_comment: Factorio name -> the pack item, tag or fluid it is on Terra (ADR-0026's conversion input).
This is a design document, not a lookup table the converter could have inlined: it is where
ADR-0021's "Terra's resources are Nauvis's resources" stops being a slogan and names items.
THE BORROW/AUTHOR RULE (ADR-0031). Borrow an existing item unless the row sits on a rung
boundary or a mod's competing line would give a parallel escape -- then author it first-party
and recipe-remove the competitor. The circuits author because they carry progression;
`copper-cable` borrows because it carries none. That rule makes most rows transcription.
THE MATERIAL FORMS ARE FTB MATERIALS' (ADR-0061). Every plate, gear, rod, wire, dust and
ingot in ADR-0021's alphabet borrows from `ftbmaterials:`; a tech mod supplies machines, not
material forms. Railcraft Reborn and Oritech each ship a competing line and AlmostUnified left
with ADR-0060, so a shared `c:` tag now resolves to two or three items: a row on a material
form names the ITEM, never the tag. `tests/pack/test_item_map.py` is the guard.
THE INPUT ALPHABET IS CLOSED (#124, amending ADR-0021). Terra's four ores -- iron, copper,
coal, uranium -- plus its stone and what its surface grows are the whole input alphabet for
every pack-authored Terra recipe. The Nether is removed, so no row may reach for redstone,
quartz, gold, lapis or diamond, and the rule binds hand-authored recipes too.
TWO KINDS OF ROW. A row either names a target or says `status: undecided` and why -- with a
`ticket` where a ticket owns the question. A missing row is a HARD FAILURE in the converter
(#72's decision): a Factorio name nobody has looked at must never be quietly skipped. An
`undecided` row is a recorded skip: the converter emits nothing for any recipe touching it
and reports the row, so the blocked set is a list rather than a silence.
A row may carry `blocked_by`, the ticket that makes its target LOADABLE: a first-party item
`planetaryfactory_core` has not registered yet, or a borrowed one whose mod is not installed on
26.1.2 (#486's machines). The target is kept as the standing
proposal. The converter skips every recipe touching one, so nothing is emitted that the game
rejects at load (#279).
A row may carry `outside_corpus`, the reason its name is in no corpus recipe: an item the pack
ships whose Factorio recipe is outside the extracted corpus, such as Space Age's turbo tier. The
converter reports each as a recorded skip, and the check fails one the corpus does name.
`kind` is `item`, `tag` or `fluid`. A tag is an ingredient-side answer only; a recipe RESULT
on a tag row cannot be emitted, because a result has to be one item.
Quantities are NOT here. Nothing is scaled: item counts transfer 1:1 and 1 mB is one Factorio

A row may carry `components`, a data-component patch on the target item -- the science packs are one `researchd:research_pack` item told apart by a component, not four items. The converter emits those as a `neoforge:components` ingredient.
fluid unit (#126, rewriting ADR-0025's table).

accumulator.note: The pack's block on Oritech's Large Energy Storage entity, placed whole on the footprint seam (ADR-0077) and mixed in to Factorio's 5 MJ and 300 kW (#283, ADR-0062).

advanced-circuit.note: As `electronic-circuit`. ADR-0031's three tiers, one item each.

arithmetic-combinator.note: A combinator decides or computes on a Redstone signal, and nothing supplies one: #148 left the row unemitted because Create's redstone line covered it, and Create left with ADR-0060 (ADR-0095). Which block it is, if any, is #484's.

assembling-machine-1.note: A `planetaryfactory_core` subclass of Oritech's machine holding a player-set recipe (ADR-0060, ADR-0071), decided by #277. The block is registered by #326, which unblocks the row; it reads `planetaryfactory:assembling` rather than Oritech's assembler type (ADR-0063).

assembling-machine-2.note: Tier 2 of the `planetaryfactory_core` Assembling Machine: a block of its own at Factorio's speed and draw, with a fluid input (ADR-0075, #295).

assembling-machine-3.note: Tier 3 of the `planetaryfactory_core` Assembling Machine (ADR-0075, #295). Registered; its recipe takes `speed-module`, undecided on #120, so the converter records it as a skip.

asteroid-collector.note: Post-launch, and `not_emitted` on its shelf; #113 and #114 own the space chapter.

automation-science-pack.note: ADR-0018's rung 1. A Researchd RESEARCH PACK, not an item of this pack's own: `kubejs/server_scripts/researchd.js` declares it with `registerResearchPacks` and the player holds `researchd:research_pack` carrying a `researchd:research_pack` data component. The declared id is `planetary_factory:` -- an underscore, and not this pack's item namespace. Registering a plain item of the same name would ship a second, inert pack the Lab cannot read.

barrel.note: ADR-0037. Registered in `planetaryfactory_core` as an `IFluidHandlerItem`: 50 mB -- Factorio's 50 units under the converter's 1:1 fluid rule -- stacking to 10, accepting any fluid. GregTech's cells were the only installed candidates and are a six-material ladder with a temperature band, for a concept that has one tier. Filled and emptied by Create's Spout and Item Drain with no recipes at all (#93), so this row is the only place the container is named.

battery.note: Factorio's battery is a crafting intermediate, not a placed power store: GregTech's batteries are tiered chargeable hulls and Electro's capacitor is a different thing, so borrowing either would put an EU container inside a recipe that wants lead and acid. Texture borrows `gtceu:max_battery`. No tier suffix -- there is one battery.

battery-equipment.note: #118 answered that the pack has combat (ADR-0054, ADR-0055), and the pack authors it; #231 owns the armour ladder and the equipment grid.

beacon.note: Do modules and beacons exist here?

belt-immunity-equipment.note: #118 answered that the pack has combat (ADR-0054, ADR-0055), and the pack authors it; #231 owns the armour ladder and the equipment grid.

big-electric-pole.note: Dropped by #147 on building the pole. A tier here is a supply footprint and nothing else: Factorio's big pole justifies its 4x4 area -- smaller than the medium pole's 7x7 -- by buying 30 tiles of wire reach, and the pack has no reach to sell. Power Grid owns transmission with catenary whose span is a property of the wire, not of the pole it hangs on, so the big pole would ship as a strictly worse medium pole. The remaining three are 5x5, 7x7 and 18x18, Factorio's own numbers. docs/factorio-mechanics.md splits the row this turns on: the supply area is `shipped`, the wire reach is `excluded`.

boiler.note: Terra's Boiler: fuel and water in, low-temperature steam out (#224, ADR-0048). It REPLACES the LP Solid Boiler this row used to point at -- ADR-0048 makes the steam chain pack-authored on two pack-owned fluids, and a GT boiler emitting `gtceu:steam` would re-open the power layer #37 removed. Third customer of the burner model the Furnace and the Burner Mining Drill share (ADR-0047): `fuel_value * effectivity` into a buffer, drained at the prototype's own draw. One tier -- ADR-0033's reactor emits superheated steam directly, so `heat-exchanger` stays on #135. Flipped from `undecided` when the block landed, not before: an item-map target for a block that does not exist emits a recipe naming nothing.

bulk-inserter.note: Beltworks' tier-4 loader, crafted from the bulk inserter's recipe and moving its tier's items a second whatever belt it is on (#347, ADR-0076). A loader is the pack's inserter: ADR-0060 replaces the swing arm with a block that loads and unloads a belt.

burner-inserter.note: Beltworks' tier-1 loader, crafted from the burner inserter's recipe and moving its tier's items a second whatever belt it is on (#347, ADR-0076). A loader is the pack's inserter: ADR-0060 replaces the swing arm with a block that loads and unloads a belt.

burner-mining-drill.note: Rung 0's rig, and `planetaryfactory_core`'s (ADR-0043, #193). GregTech owns no solid extraction on Terra: `gtceu:lv_miner` deletes an ore block whole whatever amount it held and takes its drops from the loot table, which Terra's ore blocks do not have, so it would destroy a field and pay out nothing. The rig draws one unit per operation through `OreMining` instead (ADR-0041). 2x2 over the 2x2 beneath it, burning solid fuel at 150 kW under ADR-0047, and every one of those numbers is a `data/factorio/machine.json` row. Its own recipe is Factorio's, category `crafting`, so the Personal Assembler plans it at rung 0.

car.note: Is personal transport a mechanic here?

carbon.note: The asteroid economy, `not_emitted` on its shelf.

carbonic-asteroid-chunk.note: The asteroid economy, `not_emitted` on its shelf.

cargo-bay.note: Post-launch orbit. GCyR left with ADR-0060, so the space chapter has no host mod; #340 holds the wait on Oritech: Space Age.

cargo-landing-pad.note: Post-launch orbit. GCyR left with ADR-0060, so the space chapter has no host mod; #340 holds the wait on Oritech: Space Age. Its post-launch arc is the Rocket silo row's sub-rule.

cargo-wagon.note: Railcraft Reborn's Cargo Minecart (#278): a train car that carries items.

chemical-plant.note: The pack's block on the Assembling Machine's chassis, wearing Oritech's Centrifuge model (ADR-0096, #490). Not Oritech's Centrifuge, which ADR-0060 recipe-removes as ore-doubling.

The declared id is `planetary_factory:` -- an underscore, and not this pack's item namespace. Registering a plain item of the same name would ship a second, inert pack the Lab cannot read.

concrete.note: Vanilla concrete. Factorio's concrete is a walking-speed floor; Block Runner supplies that mechanic and the colour carries the hazard fiction the texture already has.

construction-robot.note: Does the pack have robots at all?

copper-cable.note: ADR-0031 names this row: cable carries no progression, so it borrows. ADR-0061 moves the borrow to FTB Materials' `copper_wire`, which is the wire form of the alphabet's copper rather than a rung on a tech mod's ladder -- the problem the old `powergrid:wire` target had, where five wires existed and this row had to pick one.

crude-oil.note: Oritech's crude oil, the input of its Refinery's `oilbase` recipe (#277). Its near-black already reads as Factorio's. Rendered in Factorio's `base_color`: `scripts/build-fluid-tints.py` retints it where Oritech's own colour is more than 0.15 away (#277).

crude-oil-barrel.note: One container, filled by Create's Spout and drained by its Item Drain (#93). The container is `planetaryfactory:barrel` (ADR-0037).

crusher.note: Post-launch, and `not_emitted` on its shelf; #113 and #114 own the space chapter.

display-panel.note: A display panel shows a Redstone signal, and nothing supplies one since Power Grid left with ADR-0060 and Create with it (ADR-0095). Which block it is, if any, is #484's.

electric-furnace.note: The ladder's top rung (#155): `crafting_speed` 2, no fuel slot, 13 EU/t through GTCEu's `IEnergyContainer`, fed by ADR-0036's supply-area pole and by nothing else -- `acceptEnergyFromNetwork` returns 0, so a GT cable run cannot reach it. #149 specified it on a GT chassis and is closed as superseded: a GT machine reads `SmeltingRecipe` through `GTRecipeType.proxyRecipes` and would be blind to the count-bearing `planetaryfactory:smelting` type. Idle draw is not modelled (ADR-0029 excludes it).

electric-mining-drill.note: Rung 1's rig, and `planetaryfactory_core`'s (ADR-0043, #194). The burner rig's mechanism unchanged -- one unit per operation through `OreMining` (ADR-0041), the same eject -- on a 3x3 mining the 5x5 beneath it at 0.5 mining speed, and powered by standing in a supply-area pole's area (ADR-0036) at 90 kW, 45 FE/t under ADR-0060. Every one of those numbers is a `data/factorio/machine.json` row. Its own recipe is Factorio's, category `crafting`, so the Personal Assembler plans it.

electronic-circuit.note: Registered in `kubejs/startup_scripts/items.js`. #62 removed GregTech's and Mekanism's competing lines; the tier carries progression, so it authors rather than borrows.

engine-unit.note: Factorio's engine is an intermediate no installed mod ships as one item, and it feeds recipes the pack wants. ADR-0031's author case: no borrow candidate exists.

exoskeleton-equipment.note: #118 answered that the pack has combat (ADR-0054, ADR-0055), and the pack authors it; #231 owns the armour ladder and the equipment grid.

explosives.note: Every consumer is military -- grenades, mines, artillery -- so whether this row exists at all is the combat line's question, not the oil chapter's. Its only in-scope consumer is the grenade, which #230 owns.

express-splitter.note: Beltworks' tier-3 splitter: two blocks wide, two belts in and two out, splitting and merging evenly and sending everything to the free side when one backs up, each side capped at its tier's 45 items/s (#349, ADR-0076).

express-transport-belt.note: Beltworks' tier-3 belt tile, one block of belt at Factorio's 45 items/s, merged with its neighbours into one transport line (#345, ADR-0084). ADR-0060 gives item logistics to the fork, which carries the tier table.

express-underground-belt.note: Create owns item logistics (ADR-0017) and ships ONE belt: speed comes from the drivetrain's RPM, not from a faster belt item, so Factorio's three-tier ladder has no item to land on. A splitter is a funnel-and-belt arrangement and an underground belt is a belt under a block -- both are shapes the player builds, not blocks the player crafts.

fast-inserter.note: Beltworks' tier-3 loader, crafted from the fast inserter's recipe and moving its tier's items a second whatever belt it is on (#347, ADR-0076). A loader is the pack's inserter: ADR-0060 replaces the swing arm with a block that loads and unloads a belt.

fast-splitter.note: Beltworks' tier-2 splitter: two blocks wide, two belts in and two out, splitting and merging evenly and sending everything to the free side when one backs up, each side capped at its tier's 30 items/s (#349, ADR-0076).

fast-transport-belt.note: Beltworks' tier-2 belt tile, one block of belt at Factorio's 30 items/s, merged with its neighbours into one transport line (#345, ADR-0084). ADR-0060 gives item logistics to the fork, which carries the tier table.

fast-underground-belt.note: Create owns item logistics (ADR-0017) and ships ONE belt: speed comes from the drivetrain's RPM, not from a faster belt item, so Factorio's three-tier ladder has no item to land on. A splitter is a funnel-and-belt arrangement and an underground belt is a belt under a block -- both are shapes the player builds, not blocks the player crafts.

firearm-magazine.note: #118 answered that the pack has combat (ADR-0054, ADR-0055), and the pack authors it; #230 owns the combat line this row is on.

fluid-wagon.note: Railcraft Reborn's Minecart with Tank (#278): a train car that carries a fluid.

fluoroketone-cold.note: Aquilo's fluid. It reaches the corpus only through a barrel recipe, and barrelling is `native_mechanic` (#93), so nothing emitted references it.

fluoroketone-cold-barrel.note: One container, filled by Create's Spout and drained by its Item Drain (#93). The container is `planetaryfactory:barrel` (ADR-0037).

fluoroketone-hot.note: Aquilo's fluid. It reaches the corpus only through a barrel recipe, and barrelling is `native_mechanic` (#93), so nothing emitted references it.

fluoroketone-hot-barrel.note: One container, filled by Create's Spout and drained by its Item Drain (#93). The container is `planetaryfactory:barrel` (ADR-0037).

gate.note: #118 answered that the pack has combat (ADR-0054, ADR-0055), and the pack authors it; #230 owns the combat line this row is on.

grenade.note: #118 answered that the pack has combat (ADR-0054, ADR-0055), and the pack authors it; #230 owns the combat line this row is on.

gun-turret.note: #118 answered that the pack has combat (ADR-0054, ADR-0055), and the pack authors it; #230 owns the combat line this row is on.

hazard-concrete.note: `not_emitted` by #473. Factorio's hazard concrete is concrete with a striped texture that turns with the tile, and vanilla has no striped block, so a plain colour would put the name on something that does not do the thing. Colour is the recolour's instead: 10 concrete to 10 of any colour (#473).

heat-exchanger.note: `not_emitted` on its shelf; the nuclear chapter ships without a heat layer (ADR-0033).

heavy-armor.note: #118 answered that the pack has combat (ADR-0054, ADR-0055), and the pack authors it; #231 owns the armour ladder and the equipment grid.

heavy-oil.note: The heaviest of the three fractions Oritech's Refinery splits oil into -- 1000 oil to 500 heavy oil, 250 naphtha and 250 diesel, Factorio's own three-way shape (#277). Oritech draws it near-black; Factorio's is dark orange, so it is retinted. Rendered in Factorio's `base_color`: `scripts/build-fluid-tints.py` retints it where Oritech's own colour is more than 0.15 away (#277).

heavy-oil-barrel.note: One container, filled by Create's Spout and drained by its Item Drain (#93). The container is `planetaryfactory:barrel` (ADR-0037).

ice.note: The asteroid economy, `not_emitted` on its shelf.

inserter.note: Beltworks' tier-2 loader, crafted from the inserter's recipe and moving its tier's items a second whatever belt it is on (#347, ADR-0076). A loader is the pack's inserter: ADR-0060 replaces the swing arm with a block that loads and unloads a belt.

iron-chest.note: Authored in `kubejs/startup_scripts/blocks.js`, the shape #133 proved: `InventoryAttachment` plus `CustomChestMenu`, width 9 or the screen lays out wrong, six rows the ceiling, every face `[]` and never `null`. Vanilla ships one chest and no mod here ships a ladder, so Factorio's capacity progression is authored or absent. 9x4 = 36 slots.

iron-gear-wheel.note: FTB Materials' gear form (ADR-0061). A gear carries no progression and FTB Materials ships no ladder to escape onto -- it has no machines at all -- so it borrows (ADR-0031).

iron-ore.note: A tag, not an item: Terra's ore is GregTech's vein and Almost Unified may unify what it drops, so the row names the common tag rather than betting on one mod's raw ore. Ingredient side only, which is all `smelting` needs.

iron-plate.note: FTB Materials' plate form (ADR-0061: the intermediates are FTB Materials', not a tech mod's). ADR-0032: ore smelts 1:1 to plate, no ingot step. Was `gtceu:iron_plate` until ADR-0060 took GregTech out, at which point this row's smelt was rejected at datapack load.

iron-stick.note: FTB Materials' rod form -- Factorio's iron stick. As `iron-gear-wheel` (ADR-0061).

lab.note: Researchd's Lab, and #103 has it running running free without energy consumption. We will use this item but we need to either fork the mod to add energy capability or wait for an upstream update.

landfill.note: Terra is flat (ADR-0019) and has no water to fill, so the mechanic has no job here.

light-armor.note: #118 answered that the pack has combat (ADR-0054, ADR-0055), and the pack authors it; #231 owns the armour ladder and the equipment grid.

light-oil.note: The middle fraction: Oritech's Light Naphtha (#277). Its orange already reads as Factorio's light oil. Rendered in Factorio's `base_color`: `scripts/build-fluid-tints.py` retints it where Oritech's own colour is more than 0.15 away (#277).

light-oil-barrel.note: One container, filled by Create's Spout and drained by its Item Drain (#93). The container is `planetaryfactory:barrel` (ADR-0037).

locomotive.note: Railcraft Reborn's Steam Locomotive (#278, ADR-0060 gives trains to Railcraft): it burns solid fuel, as Factorio's locomotive does. The Electric Locomotive stays out -- a second locomotive with no Factorio counterpart.

logistic-science-pack.note: ADR-0018's rung 2. A Researchd RESEARCH PACK, not an item of this pack's own: `kubejs/server_scripts/researchd.js` declares it with `registerResearchPacks` and the player holds `researchd:research_pack` carrying a `researchd:research_pack` data component. The declared id is `planetary_factory:` -- an underscore, and not this pack's item namespace. Registering a plain item of the same name would ship a second, inert pack the Lab cannot read.

long-handed-inserter.note: Excluded by ADR-0076 (#347): the pack's inserter is a loader, which has no swing arm to lengthen, so a long-handed tier would be a loader with nothing to distinguish it. docs/factorio-mechanics.md records the row as `excluded`.

low-density-structure.note: Factorio fidelity: the Rocket Silo's cycle consumes Factorio's own rocket intermediates. This REVISES #41, which had the cycle take HDPE sheets directly (and whose HDPE was itself superseded by ADR-0035 -- plastic is `gtceu:polyethylene`).

lubricant.note: Oritech ships no lubricant, so this borrows the Oritech fluid whose colour is Factorio's lubricant green: Biofuel (#277). It keeps Oritech's name and its Oritech uses -- a fuel -- which is the price of borrowing rather than authoring a fluid under ADR-0031. Rendered in Factorio's `base_color`: `scripts/build-fluid-tints.py` retints it where Oritech's own colour is more than 0.15 away (#277).

lubricant-barrel.note: One container, filled by Create's Spout and drained by its Item Drain (#93). The container is `planetaryfactory:barrel` (ADR-0037).

medium-electric-pole.note: ADR-0036's supply-area pole, registered in `planetaryfactory_core` by #147. A tier is a footprint and nothing else -- it grants no voltage and changes nothing a machine receives -- so the four sit on one shelf with one process. The supply areas are Factorio's own, big pole included, which covers LESS ground than the medium one because in Factorio it buys wire reach the pack has no use for.

metallic-asteroid-chunk.note: The asteroid economy, `not_emitted` on its shelf.

military-science-pack.note: #118 answered that the pack has combat (ADR-0054, ADR-0055), and the pack authors it; Military science returns with it, and #228 owns what a sixth pack does to the ladder.

modular-armor.note: #118 answered that the pack has combat (ADR-0054, ADR-0055), and the pack authors it; #231 owns the armour ladder and the equipment grid.

night-vision-equipment.note: #118 answered that the pack has combat (ADR-0054, ADR-0055), and the pack authors it; #231 owns the armour ladder and the equipment grid.

offshore-pump.note: Where water enters the factory, and the only place it can (ADR-0050). Flipped from `undecided` when the block landed, not before: an item-map target for a block that does not exist emits a recipe naming nothing.

oil-refinery.note: A `planetaryfactory_core` subclass of Oritech's machine holding a player-set recipe (ADR-0060), decided by #277; the chassis is #486's, so the row is blocked on it. Its Oritech parent is the Refinery, whose three fractions are the oil fluid rows.

oxide-asteroid-chunk.note: The asteroid economy, `not_emitted` on its shelf.

passive-provider-chest.note: A logistic-network chest, so it exists only if logistic robots do, and #145 owns that question. #28's answer, Create 6's package logistics, left with Create (ADR-0060).

personal-roboport-equipment.note: Equipment-grid module (#231), but a personal roboport exists only if robots do, and #145 owns that question.

petroleum-gas.note: The third fraction: Oritech's Diesel (#277). NOT A GAS -- a knowing departure that keeps the three-fraction shape the oil recipes are about. Oritech draws it olive-yellow and no Oritech fluid is purple, so it is retinted to Factorio's. petroleum-gas-barrel.note: One container, filled by Create's Spout and drained by its Item Drain (#93). The container is `planetaryfactory:barrel` (ADR-0037).

piercing-rounds-magazine.note: #118 answered that the pack has combat (ADR-0054, ADR-0055), and the pack authors it; #230 owns the combat line this row is on.

pipe.note: Oritech's Fluid Pipe (#277): ADR-0060 makes Oritech the pack's tech mod, and its pipe is the plain placed pipe Factorio's is.

pipe-to-ground.note: No row is needed: the recipe is `not_emitted` (subgroup-owner.json) because underground pipes are `excluded` -- a Create pipe routes freely in three dimensions, and `create:encased_fluid_pipe` is decoration rather than a buried run.

plastic-bar.note: Plastic gates rung 2 (ADR-0025) and a rung-boundary row authors rather than borrows (ADR-0031). Its recipe is `pack:chemical_plant` and waits on #107; the ITEM exists now, so the recipes that consume it are not blocked on a machine they do not use.

power-armor.note: #118 answered that the pack has combat (ADR-0054, ADR-0055), and the pack authors it; #231 owns the armour ladder and the equipment grid.

power-switch.note: Joins or cuts two pole networks. #277 proposed `oritech:flux_gate`, which is a crafting item rather than a block, and Oritech ships no switch; a first-party block on the core's poles (ADR-0062), #294's.

production-science-pack.note: ADR-0018's rung 4. A Researchd RESEARCH PACK, not an item of this pack's own: `kubejs/server_scripts/researchd.js` declares it with `registerResearchPacks` and the player holds `researchd:research_pack` carrying a `researchd:research_pack` data component. The declared id is `planetary_factory:` -- an underscore, and not this pack's item namespace. Registering a plain item of the same name would ship a second, inert pack the Lab cannot read.

programmable-speaker.note: A programmable speaker raises an alert on a Redstone condition, and nothing supplies one since Power Grid left with ADR-0060 (ADR-0095). Which block it is, if any, is #484's.

pump.note: Factorio's in-line pump. Not `oritech:pump`, which drains fluid from the world rather than moving it along a pipe (#277). A first-party block, #293's; `offshore-pump` is already first-party (ADR-0050).

pumpjack.note: Factorio's Pumpjack (#377, ADR-0081): a 3x3x3 footprint machine standing on an oil well, drawing 45 FE/t and a 1.5 FE/t drain, and pumping 10 mB/s of crude at 100% yield out of any face. Mechanism, so `planetaryfactory_core`'s (ADR-0015). Drawn by Oritech's Pump model, scaled.

radar.note: Factorio's Radar (#368, ADR-0079): a 3x3x3 footprint machine drawing 150 FE/t that charts one 32-block sector of its reach per 10 MJ into its owner's team's chart. Mechanism, so `planetaryfactory_core`'s (ADR-0015). It detects nothing hidden: ore lies on the surface (ADR-0045).

rail.note: Vanilla rail (#277): Factorio's rail is the placed straight track, `minecraft:rail` is inside the closed input alphabet, and Railcraft Reborn builds on vanilla rails -- `railcraft:standard_rail` is a crafting component, not a track.

rail-chain-signal.note: Railcraft Reborn's Distant Signal (#278). ADAPTED -- it repeats the aspect of the signal it is linked to, which is the chain signal's look-ahead, but it reserves no path through a junction.

rail-signal.note: Railcraft Reborn's Block Signal (#277): it watches a block of track for carts, which is Factorio's rail signal.

Factorio's refined hazard concrete is refined concrete with a striped texture that turns with the tile, and vanilla has no striped block, so a plain colour would put the name on something that does not do the thing. Colour is the recolour's instead: 10 concrete to 10 of any colour (#473).

repair-pack.note: Factorio's repair pack repairs BLOCKS -- damaged entities in the world. Minecraft has no block damage to repair, and item repair is the anvil's. The mechanic has no referent here.

rocket-fuel.note: As `low-density-structure`: a solid item, Factorio's own, made from `solid-fuel` and light oil. Distinct from `gtceu:rocket_fuel`, the FLUID the GCyR rocket entity burns (#41).

rocket-part.note: Made in the Rocket Silo, which #378 authors; whether the part cycle survives is #378's question too.

rocket-silo.note: A first-party footprint machine, not waiting on Oritech: Space Age (#378). #41's GTCEu multiblock and GCyR rocket left with ADR-0060.

selector-combinator.note: As `arithmetic-combinator`. Its corpus recipe also takes five `decider-combinator`, so it waits on that row too.

shotgun.note: #118 answered that the pack has combat (ADR-0054, ADR-0055), and the pack authors it; #230 owns the combat line this row is on.

shotgun-shell.note: #118 answered that the pack has combat (ADR-0054, ADR-0055), and the pack authors it; #230 owns the combat line this row is on.

small-electric-pole.note: ADR-0036's supply-area pole, registered in `planetaryfactory_core` by #147. A tier is a footprint and nothing else -- it grants no voltage and changes nothing a machine receives -- so the four sit on one shelf with one process. The supply areas are Factorio's own, big pole included, which covers LESS ground than the medium one because in Factorio it buys wire reach the pack has no use for.

small-lamp.note: Oritech's Industrial Light, the plain placed light (#277).

solar-panel.note: Oritech's Big Solar Panel (#277). Its FE reaches the grid through a core pole, which pulls from Oritech generators (ADR-0062).

solar-panel-equipment.note: #118 answered that the pack has combat (ADR-0054, ADR-0055), and the pack authors it; #231 owns the armour ladder and the equipment grid.

solid-fuel.note: GregTech ships no solid fuel item and borrowing `minecraft:coal` would have the oil chapter print an ore the pack mines, which ADR-0032's 1:1 stance forbids. Burnable, made from the oil fractions in the Chemical Plant. Feeds `rocket-fuel`.

space-platform-foundation.note: Post-launch orbit. GCyR left with ADR-0060, so the space chapter has no host mod; #340 holds the wait on Oritech: Space Age.

space-platform-starter-pack.note: Post-launch orbit. GCyR left with ADR-0060, so the space chapter has no host mod; #340 holds the wait on Oritech: Space Age.

space-science-pack.note: Made in orbit in Space Age, so it waits on the platform: Post-launch orbit. GCyR left with ADR-0060, so the space chapter has no host mod; #340 holds the wait on Oritech: Space Age.

splitter.note: Beltworks' tier-1 splitter: two blocks wide, two belts in and two out, splitting and merging evenly and sending everything to the free side when one backs up, each side capped at its tier's 15 items/s (#349, ADR-0076).

steam-engine.note: A `planetaryfactory_core` block on Oritech's Steam Engine entity, placed from one item as its whole footprint and broken as one (ADR-0077, #352). Oritech's chaining, fill-driven speed and efficiency curve are kept, with a mixin putting Factorio's rate in place of Oritech's arithmetic -- 30 mB/s and 450 FE/t at the curve's peak, no water returned (ADR-0062). The recipe is Factorio's, emitted by the converter; Oritech's own engine and its crafting recipe are swept (ADR-0034).

steel-chest.note: Authored in `kubejs/startup_scripts/blocks.js`, the shape #133 proved: `InventoryAttachment` plus `CustomChestMenu`, width 9 or the screen lays out wrong, six rows the ceiling, every face `[]` and never `null`. Vanilla ships one chest and no mod here ships a ladder, so Factorio's capacity progression is authored or absent. 9x6 = 54 slots, the ceiling.

steel-furnace.note: The furnace ladder is `planetaryfactory_core`'s: three blocks reading the pack's own count-bearing `planetaryfactory:smelting` and nothing else (#155). Vanilla's furnace consumes exactly one item and Factorio's steel is 5 plates, so the count is the reason the type exists; the vanilla type is not read alongside it, because ADR-0034's sweep leaves it with no live recipe. Speed and fuel only, gating nothing (#91). Fuel-burning, `crafting_speed` 2. Blast furnace texture.

steel-plate.note: The only surviving alloy on Terra -- iron plus coal, #72. FTB Materials' plate form (ADR-0061); note that FTB Materials also ships a `steel_ingot`, and this row is deliberately the PLATE, because ADR-0032 removed the ingot step from Terra's chain entirely. Its `smelting` recipe is 5 plates to 1, which no vanilla shape can express; it rides the count-bearing `planetaryfactory:smelting` type, which #155 landed.

stone.note: Factorio's stone is the MINED rock, and Minecraft's mined rock is cobblestone. Amends the earlier reading (`minecraft:stone`), which took the smelted block for the raw one and left `stone-brick` nowhere faithful to land.

stone-brick.note: Factorio's stone brick is a building material -- walls, floors, the furnaces themselves -- and Minecraft's building block of that name is `minecraft:stone_bricks`. The recipe is the corpus verbatim: 2 stone to 1, category `smelting`, which no vanilla furnace shape can express, so it rides the count-bearing `planetaryfactory:smelting` type with `steel-plate`, which #155 landed. ADR-0046 reversed the earlier reading (`minecraft:stone` on a 1:1 vanilla shape), which only ever worked by putting the item on the smelted block.

stone-furnace.note: The furnace ladder is `planetaryfactory_core`'s: three blocks reading the pack's own count-bearing `planetaryfactory:smelting` and nothing else (#155). Vanilla's furnace consumes exactly one item and Factorio's steel is 5 plates, so the count is the reason the type exists; the vanilla type is not read alongside it, because ADR-0034's sweep leaves it with no live recipe. Speed and fuel only, gating nothing (#91). Rung 0, fuel-burning, `crafting_speed` 1. Vanilla's furnace recipe goes with the stock sweep.

stone-wall.note: #118 answered that the pack has combat (ADR-0054, ADR-0055), and the pack authors it; #230 owns the combat line this row is on.

storage-tank.note: Oritech's Portable Tank, its one placeable fluid tank (#277). Railcraft's tanks are a coloured multiblock with no single item. FIDELITY NOTE: a Factorio storage tank is a 3x3 of a fixed size; this is one block with Oritech's capacity. Accepted: the recipe is the corpus's, the capacity Oritech's.

submachine-gun.note: #118 answered that the pack has combat (ADR-0054, ADR-0055), and the pack authors it; #230 owns the combat line this row is on.

substation.note: ADR-0036's supply-area pole, registered in `planetaryfactory_core` by #147. A tier is a footprint and nothing else -- it grants no voltage and changes nothing a machine receives -- so the four sit on one shelf with one process. The supply areas are Factorio's own, big pole included, which covers LESS ground than the medium one because in Factorio it buys wire reach the pack has no use for.

sulfur.note: FTB Materials' dust form (ADR-0061). Its RECIPE is `pack:chemical_plant` and waits on #107.

sulfuric-acid.note: Oritech's Sulfuric Acid (#277). Oritech draws it bright green; Factorio's is yellow, so it is retinted. Rendered in Factorio's `base_color`: `scripts/build-fluid-tints.py` retints it where Oritech's own colour is more than 0.15 away (#277).

sulfuric-acid-barrel.note: One container, filled by Create's Spout and drained by its Item Drain (#93). The container is `planetaryfactory:barrel` (ADR-0037).

train-stop.note: Railcraft Reborn's Iron Buffer Stop Track (#277): the end of the line a train is stopped at. ADAPTED -- Factorio's stop is also a schedule target by name, which a buffer stop is not.

transport-belt.note: Beltworks' tier-1 belt tile, one block of belt at Factorio's 15 items/s, merged with its neighbours into one transport line (#345, ADR-0084). ADR-0060 gives item logistics to the fork, which carries the tier table.

turbo-splitter.note: Beltworks' tier-4 splitter: two blocks wide, two belts in and two out, splitting and merging evenly and sending everything to the free side when one backs up, each side capped at its tier's 60 items/s (#349, ADR-0076).
turbo-splitter.outside_corpus: Space Age's recipe, which needs tungsten plate from Vulcanus; the corpus is Nauvis pre-launch (#72), so the splitter ships with no recipe (#341).

turbo-transport-belt.note: Beltworks' tier-4 belt tile, one block of belt at Factorio's 60 items/s, merged with its neighbours into one transport line (#345, ADR-0084). ADR-0060 gives item logistics to the fork, which carries the tier table.
turbo-transport-belt.outside_corpus: Space Age's recipe, which needs tungsten plate from Vulcanus; the corpus is Nauvis pre-launch (#72), so the belt ships with no recipe (#341).

underground-belt.note: Excluded by ADR-0044, restated by ADR-0060: an underground solves weaving past another belt in two dimensions, and Minecraft has a Y axis. Tile belts are flat (ADR-0084), so whether a belt crosses another by climbing over it is #412's. The SimpleBelts fork ships none. docs/factorio-mechanics.md records the sub-rule as `excluded`.

uranium-ore.note: Raw Uranium, what a pack uranium ore block pays out (#321). FTB Materials' raw form (ADR-0061); its ore blocks are not used, since a block has to carry an amount (ADR-0041).

utility-science-pack.note: Not a space item: ADR-0018 reserves it for after the first launch, and #139 owns the post-launch production rung.

water.note: Vanilla water. 1 mB is 1 Factorio fluid unit (#126).

water-barrel.note: One container, filled by Create's Spout and drained by its Item Drain (#93). The container is `planetaryfactory:barrel` (ADR-0037).

wood.note: Factorio's tree drops `wood` directly with no intermediate, so a LOG is Factorio's wood. A tag, because no single species is the pack's. This row read `minecraft:planks` until ADR-0039: log-to-planks is a vanilla shaped recipe, so ADR-0034's sweep removes it, #140 removes the 2x2 that would make it, #97 forbids re-emitting it, and the corpus has no plank to author -- planks were unobtainable, which made the Engineer's Iron Pick unbuildable. Moves `small-electric-pole` and `wooden-chest` with it.

wooden-chest.note: Vanilla's chest is Factorio's wooden chest with no argument to have about it. Vanilla's OWN shaped recipe still exists until the stock-recipe sweep (#143) removes it; leaving both would be two ways to make one thing, which ADR-0017's losing-recipe-is-removed idiom forbids. This recipe is not itself a vanilla shaped recipe, so #97 is satisfied either way.
